title.zh: Slippery slop：代码质量与控制权
title.en: Slippery slop: code quality and control

sourceText:
Good morning from Vienna People of Pi🌞 Sunday meditations today from

@badlogicgames and @mitsuhiko 

Among other things: 
- agents that generate too much code poison their own  context (slippery slop)
- code matters wherever control matters
- unreadable code from Astra

zh.title: 代码越多，agent 自己也越难工作
zh.text: 两人认为，模型大量生成代码会占用有限的上下文，进一步放大质量问题。即使并非所有实现都值得逐行关注，关键基础设施、接口和类型仍需要人的控制。

zh.title: 可读性下降会削弱人的参与
zh.text: Armin 描述 Astra 生成过度压缩的代码与工具调用，让他越来越不愿意阅读。他们提出训练目标可能存在冲突，但明确表示原因尚不确定。

zh.title: 测试通过不能替代理解
zh.text: 即使有很高的覆盖率，也不等于覆盖所有重要输入。难读的实现让人更难判断测试是否充分，测试容易变成只有心理安慰的形式。

zh.title: 不同模型能否承担不同职责
zh.text: 两人探讨让一个模型负责工具调用、另一个负责实现的可能性。这是一种待验证的设想，并非已经得到证实的解决办法。

zh.title: 更多产出是否带来更多用户价值
zh.text: 对话区分了 token 消耗、提交数量与真正有价值的产品改进。Mario 更希望利用 agent 在相近交付速度下提高质量，而不是无限增加功能。

zh.title: 漏洞发现与修复能力并不同步
zh.text: 他们讨论自动化安全研究的两面性：旧软件可能因此修复更多漏洞，但攻击门槛也下降，而验证与应用补丁仍消耗人的时间。

en.title: More code can make the agent’s own job harder
en.text: They argue that excessive generated code consumes limited context and compounds quality problems. Critical infrastructure, interfaces and types still need human control even when not every implementation deserves line-by-line attention.

en.title: Poor readability pushes people away from the code
en.text: Armin describes compressed Astra code and tool calls that discourage inspection. They consider possible conflicts in training objectives, while making clear that the cause is uncertain.

en.title: Passing tests do not replace understanding
en.text: High coverage does not guarantee coverage of every important input. Unreadable implementations make test adequacy harder to judge, allowing tests to become reassurance without sufficient scrutiny.

en.title: Could different models take different roles?
en.text: They explore using one model for tool calls and another for implementation. This is a possible experiment, rather than an established solution.

en.title: More output does not necessarily mean more value
en.text: The discussion separates token spending and commit counts from meaningful product improvements. Mario would prefer similar delivery speed with higher quality over an endless expansion of features.

en.title: Finding vulnerabilities and fixing them scale differently
en.text: Automated security research may produce more fixes in established software, while also lowering the barrier to attack. Verifying and applying patches still takes human effort.

segments.text: But you can't be loud.
segments.zh: 但你不能大声。

segments.text: Be quiet with the sword.
segments.zh: 拿着剑的时候安静一点。

segments.text: Be quiet with the sword.
segments.zh: 拿着剑的时候安静一点。

segments.text: Code is less important than it used to be, obviously.
segments.zh: 显然，代码已经没有以前那么重要了。

segments.text: But the question is, how good can your agent deal with a shit ton of code,
segments.zh: 但问题是，面对这么一大堆代码，你的 agent 到底能处理得多好？

segments.text: given its limitations with respect to context window?
segments.zh: 毕竟它的上下文窗口是有限的。

segments.text: So the agent is ultimately hurting itself by generating too much code.
segments.zh: 所以，生成太多代码，到头来是在坑它自己。

segments.text: Is the code as important as it used to be?
segments.zh: 代码还像以前一样重要吗？

segments.text: No, definitely not.
segments.zh: 不，肯定没那么重要了。

segments.text: But I would say that it is still important in Astra is cool and all,
segments.zh: 但我觉得代码仍然重要。Astra 很酷，

segments.text: just like Fable, but there's still slot machines.
segments.zh: Fable 也是，但它们仍然像老虎机。

segments.text: And I would say there is a lot of code where you don't need to know what it does and how it works.
segments.zh: 确实有很多代码，你不需要知道它具体做什么、怎么工作。

segments.text: But there's also a lot of very important infrastructure code where you still want to know what it does.
segments.zh: 但也有很多重要的基础设施代码，你还是得知道它在做什么。

segments.text: I think ultimately it comes down to control.
segments.zh: 归根结底，这是控制权的问题。

segments.text: I personally like controlling interfaces and types.
segments.zh: 我个人喜欢把接口和类型掌握在自己手里。

segments.text: And as long as I have control of that, the LLM is kind of limited in how much damage it can do.
segments.zh: 只要这些还在我的控制之下，LLM 能造成的破坏就比较有限。

segments.text: Yes, the models can shit out immense amounts of code now, but by doing so, they're hurting themselves because ultimately they still have a limited context window.
segments.zh: 没错，模型现在能疯狂吐出大量代码，但这也在坑自己，因为它们的上下文窗口终究有限。

segments.text: And if it doesn't fit, you get more slop.
segments.zh: 一旦装不下，就会冒出更多垃圾代码。

segments.text: What I found interesting with the Astra release is that I,
segments.zh: Astra 发布后，我发现一件很有意思的事：

segments.text: for the first time, felt like less and less desire to actually look at the code that it produces because it's so hard to see.
segments.zh: 我第一次越来越不想看它生成的代码，因为实在太难看了。

segments.text: And not, I mean, it's hard to look at.
segments.zh: 我是说，看着就很费劲。

segments.text: It is incredibly compressed in situations in where it shouldn't be,
segments.zh: 它会在不该压缩的地方，把代码压得特别紧，

segments.text: even when it actually uses code generation for writing code.
segments.zh: 甚至在正经生成代码时也是这样。

segments.text: But it's particularly unreadable when it uses code to call tools.
segments.zh: 而用代码调用工具时，尤其难读。

segments.text: So like actually following along what it's doing is also getting harder and harder just by how it writes code.
segments.zh: 光是它写代码的方式，就让人越来越难跟上它在做什么。

segments.text: And I think like to Mario's point, like it actually does get, like during the training process,
segments.zh: 就像 Mario 说的，在训练过程中，

segments.text: it probably gets rewarded for token efficiency.
segments.zh: 它可能会因为节省 token 而获得奖励。

segments.text: But as a result of this token efficiency, it is hard to read.
segments.zh: 但追求这种 token 效率的结果，就是难以阅读。

segments.text: And there's a tension, I think, sort of forming where I think even if you get the
segments.zh: 我觉得这里出现了一种矛盾：即使你把

segments.text: interfaces right and everything else, like if I look at an Astra produced code,
segments.zh: 接口之类的都设计好了，看到 Astra 生成的代码时，

segments.text: I feel an urge to do code formatting.
segments.zh: 我还是忍不住想给它格式化。

segments.text: Which I didn't feel for a very, very long time.
segments.zh: 我已经很久很久没有这种感觉了。

segments.text: I basically haven't used code formats at all because I felt like the LLM is going to follow along the style of the code that's already there.
segments.zh: 我基本没用过代码格式化工具，因为我觉得 LLM 会跟着现有代码的风格来写。

segments.text: And now it doesn't.
segments.zh: 但现在它不跟了。

segments.text: Yeah, and it is kind of odd.
segments.zh: 是啊，挺奇怪的。

segments.text: It is really odd.
segments.zh: 真的很奇怪。

segments.text: And I don't know where it's going.
segments.zh: 我也不知道接下来会怎样。

segments.text: But I'm a little bit feeling like this might become more of a thing now.
segments.zh: 但我隐约觉得，这种情况可能会越来越常见。

segments.text: And I don't know how I feel about this.
segments.zh: 我不知道该怎么看待它。

segments.text: You said something earlier, which I thought was interesting.
segments.zh: 你之前说了一点，我觉得很有意思。

segments.text: As the models are trained to not only be coding agents,
segments.zh: 模型不只被训练成编程 agent，

segments.text: but also like personal open claw-like assistants, it's that's a reason that the training might
segments.zh: 也被训练成像 OpenClaw 那样的个人助手，所以训练里可能

segments.text: contain traces or things like just create whatever the
segments.zh: 会有这样的轨迹或要求：随便写什么

segments.text: fucking code you want to create, as long as it does the thing the user asked for.
segments.zh: 破代码都行，只要完成用户要的事情。

segments.text: And the user is a non-technical user and the user doesn't write production systems,
segments.zh: 而那个用户不是技术人员，也不写生产系统，

segments.text: but just tiny little things like build me a daily news brief website or something.
segments.zh: 只是做些小东西，比如“帮我做一个每日新闻简报网站”。

segments.text: Or Minecraft clone or anything.
segments.zh: 或者仿个 Minecraft，什么都行。

segments.text: So if the models are now being trained to produce slop code just to make their users happy,
segments.zh: 所以，如果模型现在被训练成只要让用户满意，就可以生成粗糙代码，

segments.text: which is totally fine, then we'll have a detrimental effect on using these models for production software.
segments.zh: 这本身也没问题，但会损害它们用于生产软件开发的效果。

segments.text: So what I found quite interesting was,
segments.zh: 我觉得很有意思的一点是，

segments.text: I noticed as you sort of look into the code that it produces,
segments.zh: 仔细看它生成的代码，

segments.text: like in tests, in shaders, in embedded JavaScript,
segments.zh: 比如测试、着色器、嵌入的 JavaScript，

segments.text: you can clearly notice that it's way worse than in the regular code that it writes.
segments.zh: 你能明显看出这些比它平时写的普通代码差得多。

segments.text: So I wrote in a blog post, I think it's like one step removed from regular code.
segments.zh: 我在博客里写过：好像只要偏离常规代码一层，

segments.text: It sort of starts falling into this pattern of really highly compressed things.
segments.zh: 它就开始陷入那种把东西压得特别紧的模式。

segments.text: But then I was like, okay, maybe this just happens to me.
segments.zh: 但我又想，也许只有我遇到这种情况。

segments.text: So I asked a bunch of people on Twitter, like, hey, if you build like an Astro game over the weekend and it works for you,
segments.zh: 于是我在 Twitter 上问大家：如果你周末用 Astra 做了个游戏，而且觉得效果不错，

segments.text: just show me the code.
segments.zh: 就把代码给我看看。

segments.text: And there were two people who replied like, oh yeah, it wasn't so bad.
segments.zh: 有两个人回复说：“还好吧，没那么差。”

segments.text: And I just opened the code and it was really, really bad.
segments.zh: 结果我打开一看，代码真的非常糟。

segments.text: And then it was, I think both of them replied, yeah, it's probably not nice.
segments.zh: 后来他们好像也都说：“嗯，可能确实不太好看。”

segments.text: The thing is, like, we don't really expect it to actually write code this bad, I think.
segments.zh: 问题在于，我觉得我们原本没想到它真会把代码写得这么差。

segments.text: Like, I got fully trusted that the models are at least certain level of,
segments.zh: 我原本完全相信，模型至少能达到某种

segments.text: like, passing bar.
segments.zh: 及格水平。

segments.text: And it feels a little bit like it violated this now.
segments.zh: 可现在感觉它连这条底线都突破了。

segments.text: I don't know.
segments.zh: 我也说不准。

segments.text: It definitely feels like a shift.
segments.zh: 但确实感觉发生了变化。

segments.text: Yeah, just yesterday I did some work on an old C, C++ code base in Spine.
segments.zh: 对，就在昨天，我在 Spine 的一个老 C、C++ 代码库里做修改。

segments.text: I switched back to 5.6 Sol
segments.zh: 我又换回了 5.6 Sol，

segments.text: because Astro just couldn't write any sensible kind of code.
segments.zh: 因为 Astra 就是写不出什么像样的代码。

segments.text: It's very weird.
segments.zh: 很奇怪。

segments.text: It's very, very weird.
segments.zh: 真的非常奇怪。

segments.text: I blame personality fans.
segments.zh: 我怪那些追捧模型个性的人。

segments.text: One thought that I had was that if you have the idea,
segments.zh: 我想到一点：假如你认为，

segments.text: at least in theory, that you don't have to at all consider the code because,
segments.zh: 至少理论上，根本不用关心代码本身，

segments.text: like, the test coverage is going to guarantee you that the code works perfectly.
segments.zh: 因为测试覆盖率能保证代码完美运行。

segments.text: Then, even if you have, like, 100% branch coverage,
segments.zh: 那么，就算分支覆盖率达到了 100%，

segments.text: which I don't think is likely, do your reader cover all the possible inputs to that function?
segments.zh: 虽然我觉得这不太可能，你真的覆盖了这个函数所有可能的输入吗？

segments.text: And one of the things that I noticed, like, with this is that because it
segments.zh: 我注意到的一点是，它把代码

segments.text: compresses the code so much, I,
segments.zh: 压缩得太厉害了，

segments.text: when I just look at the diff that it does, I don't have any confidence that,
segments.zh: 光看它生成的 diff，我根本没有把握，

segments.text: like, I could even without asking the LLM tell you if the tests are sufficient.
segments.zh: 能在不问 LLM 的情况下判断测试到底够不够。

segments.text: I'm really struggling with this whole thing because,
segments.zh: 这整件事让我很苦恼。

segments.text: like, if the code is too unreadable, then, and I'm not saying,
segments.zh: 如果代码太难读——我不是说

segments.text: like, it's completely unreadable, but, like, it becomes so that you're one step further away from it.
segments.zh: 完全读不懂，而是你离代码又远了一层——

segments.text: And then you rely more on, like, okay, but there are tests and the tests pass and I can still navigate in my slop game.
segments.zh: 你就会更依赖这种想法：“有测试，测试都过了，我那个粗糙游戏也还能玩。”

segments.text: And so, surely the whole thing must be working.
segments.zh: 所以整套东西肯定没问题吧。

segments.text: But it's, like, it becomes so much harder to understand if you feel repulsed looking at the code.
segments.zh: 可如果代码让你看着就抗拒，理解它就会困难得多。

segments.text: So, at that point, the tests also just become performative, right?
segments.zh: 到这一步，测试也变成了做样子，对吧？

segments.text: It just gives you a good feeling of there are tests.
segments.zh: 它只是让你觉得：“有测试，挺好。”

segments.text: I don't fucking know what they do and if they actually cover what we need to cover in the tests, but they exist.
segments.zh: 我压根不知道它们在测什么，有没有覆盖该测的东西，反正它们存在。

segments.text: And that's why I feel good.
segments.zh: 所以我就放心了。

segments.text: It's very emotion-based, all of it.
segments.zh: 全都是在靠感觉。

segments.text: But if they produce code that is unreadable, then you have even less incentive of checking whether the code they produced makes any kind of fucking sense.
segments.zh: 如果生成的代码让人读不下去，你就更不想检查它到底有没有道理了。

segments.text: So, it feels like we are getting pushed to being removed from the code.
segments.zh: 感觉我们正在被一步步推离代码。

segments.text: Okay.
segments.zh: 好。

segments.text: What if you use something like Astra, which is clearly,
segments.zh: 如果用 Astra 这样的模型，它显然

segments.text: like, trained to succeed,
segments.zh: 就是被训练来把事做成的，

segments.text: but you use it only for the tool calls.
segments.zh: 但你只让它负责调用工具呢？

segments.text: Like, you don't use it for the writing.
segments.zh: 不让它负责写代码。

segments.text: So, like, whenever it tries to write some code, you're like, oh, you stop.
segments.zh: 每当它要写代码，你就说：“停下。”

segments.text: Some agent, I don't know, something else you implement now.
segments.zh: 换个 agent，或者别的什么东西来实现。

segments.text: Because I really feel like there's a tension in the training process.
segments.zh: 因为我真的觉得训练过程里存在冲突。

segments.text: They're like, either this is really good and we should like this because,
segments.zh: 要么，这种做法确实很好，我们就应该接受，

segments.text: I don't know, software engineering is solved and it's just a bug fix that we have to deal with now.
segments.zh: 比如软件工程已经解决了，眼下只剩修修补补。

segments.text: And so, we don't look at the code anymore.
segments.zh: 那我们就不再看代码了。

segments.text: So, it doesn't matter how it looks.
segments.zh: 代码长什么样也就不重要。

segments.text: And it's, like, really purely optimized for the LLM.
segments.zh: 完全针对 LLM 优化就好。

segments.text: Or, these models are actually only behaving this way because they're being trained to do other things,
segments.zh: 要么，模型之所以这样，只是因为它们被训练去做其他事情，

segments.text: particularly really good tool calling using code.
segments.zh: 尤其是很擅长用代码调用工具。

segments.text: And so, there's a tension in the training process and you should actually use a different model that's being trained to be an
segments.zh: 那么训练目标就存在冲突，你应该换个专门被训练成

segments.text: expert software engineer.
segments.zh: 优秀软件工程师的模型。

segments.text: And I really don't know what the answer is here because,
segments.zh: 我真的不知道答案是什么。

segments.text: like, it's not like you go to OpenAI page and it's like, yeah, do that.
segments.zh: 毕竟你打开 OpenAI 的网页，也不会看到它明确告诉你该这么做。

segments.text: No, but maybe that's like a model capacity issue now.
segments.zh: 不过，也许现在碰到的是模型容量的问题。

segments.text: Like, as they try to accommodate more and more use cases or vertical slices of
segments.zh: 随着模型试图覆盖越来越多用例，或越来越多

segments.text: specific industries, obviously, the model needs to know about how to operate within these environments.
segments.zh: 垂直行业，它显然就得学会如何在这些环境里工作。

segments.text: But that will ultimately mean that there are less parameters available to the things they used to be good
segments.zh: 那最终就意味着，留给它原本擅长的事情的参数变少了，

segments.text: for, like software engineering.
segments.zh: 比如软件工程。

segments.text: So, maybe we are hitting that now.
segments.zh: 也许我们现在就撞上这个问题了。

segments.text: Maybe it's the, you're trying to accommodate as many industries as possible.
segments.zh: 也许是因为想尽可能覆盖所有行业，

segments.text: So, your industry, specifically the software industry, is now suffering because there's not enough parameters left for your specific industry.
segments.zh: 结果你所在的行业，尤其是软件行业，分到的参数不够，效果就受损了。

segments.text: I don't know.
segments.zh: 我也不知道。

segments.text: The token spent on engineering went
segments.zh: 工程方面的 token 消耗，

segments.text: up in a certain way.
segments.zh: 一直在增长。

segments.text: So, you could see, like, month by month what that was.
segments.zh: 你可以逐月看到这个变化。

segments.text: But none of the top line numbers moved up at all.
segments.zh: 但那些顶线数字完全没有上涨，

segments.text: In a way, that was correlatable to this.
segments.zh: 至少看不出跟它有什么关联。

segments.text: But obviously, the number of commits went up.
segments.zh: 当然，提交次数增加了。

segments.text: The number of, like, other things that you could measure went up.
segments.zh: 其他一些能统计的数量也增加了。

segments.text: And so, it went from, like, an insignificant part of, like, the expenditure of the company to a really meaningful part of the expenditure of the company.
segments.zh: 这笔支出从公司开销里微不足道的一项，变成了相当可观的一项。

segments.text: And it might just be that we haven't figured out yet how to make that work.
segments.zh: 也许只是我们还没弄明白，怎么真正把它用好。

segments.text: Or, like, what is being produced actually isn't that much
segments.zh: 也可能只是整体来看，产出的东西并没有

segments.text: more meaningful overall.
segments.zh: 多出那么多实际价值。

segments.text: And so, because now everybody, like, as an example, like, the baseline expectation that we
segments.zh: 比如，现在大家对一款软件的基本期待，

segments.text: have now for a piece of software is that it does more.
segments.zh: 已经变成它必须做更多事情。

segments.text: So, you need now to compete with everybody else who's in your space as well.
segments.zh: 你还得跟同一领域里的其他所有人竞争。

segments.text: So, like, of course, your thing now should have a chatbot in it.
segments.zh: 所以，你的产品当然也得有聊天机器人。

segments.text: Of course, there should be, I don't know, like, the UI should behave in a certain way that was previously not necessary.
segments.zh: 界面当然也得做到一些以前根本不需要的东西。

segments.text: Like, more people now build mobile apps, I think, than they did before just because it became easier.
segments.zh: 我觉得现在做移动应用的人也比以前多了，因为门槛降低了。

segments.text: So, maybe this is sort of, like, a really weird form of, like, we are required to build more.
segments.zh: 也许这是一种很奇怪的局面：我们被要求做得更多，

segments.text: But, like, the amount of consumers is still the same.
segments.zh: 但消费者的数量还是那么多。

segments.text: So, it just has become more expensive to the software engineering.
segments.zh: 结果只是软件工程变得更贵了。

segments.text: I don't know if that's the answer.
segments.zh: 我不知道这是不是答案。

segments.text: I mean, I guess it's hard to measure at the moment just because
segments.zh: 我觉得现在也很难衡量，毕竟

segments.text: of the economic turmoil overall with oil being up and so on and so forth.
segments.zh: 整体经济不太平，油价上涨，还有各种其他因素。

segments.text: So, just taking GDP is probably a bad, bad idea.
segments.zh: 所以，单看 GDP 大概很不合适。

segments.text: But if you look at individual companies, I don't see them producing more meaningful features for the users if you're looking at software companies.
segments.zh: 但看具体公司，尤其是软件公司，我没看到它们为用户做出更多真正有意义的功能。

segments.text: I just don't see it.
segments.zh: 我真的没看到。

segments.text: Like, can you name a single software or SaaS product that has meaningfully changed in the past 12 months?
segments.zh: 你能说出哪款软件或 SaaS 产品，在过去十二个月里发生了实质变化吗？

segments.text: I mean, I think in the AI space, you see that a little bit.
segments.zh: 我觉得在 AI 领域，多少还是能看到一点。

segments.text: Yeah, but then the question is, who is using all of that stuff from the AI space?
segments.zh: 对，但问题是，AI 领域做出来的这些东西，到底谁在用？

segments.text: Yeah.
segments.zh: 是啊。

segments.text: I found, like, iOS 27 to be an interesting proof point here because,
segments.zh: 我觉得 iOS 27 就是个挺有意思的例子，

segments.text: like, clearly there should be more people in Apple using AI tools.
segments.zh: 因为苹果内部使用 AI 工具的人显然应该更多了。

segments.text: Like, I heard from people at Apple that there is, like, plenty amount of, like, AI supports of engineering going on.
segments.zh: 我听苹果的人说，他们确实在大量使用 AI 辅助开发。

segments.text: But, like, from iOS 26 to 27, I felt like it was the most
segments.zh: 但从 iOS 26 到 27，我感觉这是最

segments.text: boring iOS release.
segments.zh: 无聊的一次 iOS 更新。

segments.text: Like, if anything, it's sort of the push against this in a way.
segments.zh: 某种程度上，它反倒像是在反驳这种说法。

segments.text: I mean, I don't think that's bad, actually.
segments.zh: 其实我不觉得这是坏事。

segments.text: I don't want a Cambrian explosion of new features and the home of Simpsons car, right?
segments.zh: 我不想看到功能像寒武纪大爆发一样疯长，最后做出荷马·辛普森那辆车。

segments.text: But then I must wonder, does the additional resources that you have through agentic coding just ensure that
segments.zh: 但这样我就得问：agent 编程带来的额外资源，是否至少能确保

segments.text: whatever you push out has higher quality?
segments.zh: 交付出来的东西质量更高？

segments.text: I would like to think so.
segments.zh: 我希望如此。

segments.text: I personally would like to use agents in a way where I can say,
segments.zh: 我个人希望这样使用 agent：

segments.text: okay, my velocity is kind of the same, but everything I release is actually of higher quality,
segments.zh: 交付速度大致不变，但发布的每样东西质量都更高，

segments.text: even if the quantity stays kind of the same.
segments.zh: 即便数量基本一样。

segments.text: That would be the goal for me when using agentic engineering tools.
segments.zh: 这才是我使用 agent 工程工具想达到的目标。

segments.text: But I'm not sure if you're seeing that either, if you look at companies with their 999s going into the
segments.zh: 但我也不知道有没有改善。看看这些公司的可用性指标，原来的几个九……

segments.text: 9100 territory.
segments.zh: ［此处可用性数字转写不清，待回听］

segments.text: I think where you see it a little bit in terms of,
segments.zh: 我觉得在质量方面，可能有一点体现，

segments.text: like, quality, presumably, like, depending on how you look at this, is that software should become more secure because we are having
segments.zh: 当然也取决于你怎么看：软件应该更安全了，因为我们不得不

segments.text: to work on all of the security reports.
segments.zh: 处理所有这些安全报告。

segments.text: Right?
segments.zh: 对吧？

segments.text: And I think, like...
segments.zh: 而且我觉得……

segments.text: Well, that's not happening, I can tell you from first-hand experience.
segments.zh: 但并没有。我可以用亲身经历告诉你。

segments.text: It's definitely not more secure.
segments.zh: 它绝对没有更安全。

segments.text: But it's also riskier to be on the internet now with software.
segments.zh: 但现在把软件放到互联网上，风险确实也更高了。

segments.text: One of our colleagues, like, he's a little bit more now worried about,
segments.zh: 我们有个同事，现在更担心

segments.text: like, smart contracts and crypto wallets just because they have become such attractive targets for
segments.zh: 智能合约和加密钱包了，因为它们已经成了

segments.text: automated security research.
segments.zh: 自动化安全研究特别有吸引力的目标。

segments.text: But,
segments.zh: 不过，

segments.text: I mean, there are definitely certain areas where, like, on average,
segments.zh: 我觉得确实有一些领域，平均来说，

segments.text: like, there should be more fixes going into, like, curl is a good example,
segments.zh: 应该修掉了更多问题。curl 就是个很好的例子，

segments.text: or, like, other software.
segments.zh: 还有其他软件。

segments.text: This is really, really old.
segments.zh: 这些软件已经存在非常久了。

segments.text: So, they got a lot more valid security reports, so they fixed them.
segments.zh: 它们收到了更多有效的安全报告，于是修复了这些问题。

segments.text: So, like, in general, curl is probably safer now than it ever was.
segments.zh: 总体来说，curl 现在可能比以往任何时候都安全。

segments.text: And it doesn't slop a ton of new features into it.
segments.zh: 而且它也没有往里面塞一大堆粗糙的新功能。

segments.text: But also, the risk profile just went up simultaneously because of the same thing that...
segments.zh: 但与此同时，同样的原因也提高了整体风险……

segments.text: And that is the problem, because the security patches still take humans to verify and apply.
segments.zh: 问题就在这里：安全补丁仍然要靠人来验证和应用。

segments.text: But finding the security vulnerabilities is now, like, 100x easier.
segments.zh: 可发现漏洞，现在却容易了一百倍。

segments.text: I literally just had my clanker kind of try to break the DRM of one of my old
segments.zh: 我刚让我的“铁皮脑袋”试着破解一个老产品的

segments.text: products, and it just did it.
segments.zh: DRM，结果它就真做到了。

segments.text: It just, like, without intervention from my end.
segments.zh: 完全没用我干预。

segments.text: So, yeah, interesting times.
segments.zh: 所以，真是个有意思的时代。
